scenario.title: Wafer Sample Transfer and Disposal Request
scenario.initial_description: Samples are moved when they are needed for evaluation. After evaluation, unnecessary samples are checked and disposed of through a request process.

reference_workflow.goal: Move required wafer samples for evaluation and dispose of completed samples through traceable approval.

activities.name: Identify required sample and evaluation purpose
Submit disposal request for completed sample

decisions.condition: Is the sample available and correctly identified?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Transfer request fields can be pre-filled from sample identifiers and evaluation purpose.
Status updates can be prompted automatically after scheduled evaluation completion.
Disposal candidates can be suggested when retention conditions are not met.

activities.name: Review Evaluation Results
outputs: List of samples flagged for disposal

activities.name: Initiate Disposal Request
inputs: List of samples flagged for disposal

activities.name: Update Sample Inventory and Close Records

decisions.condition: Is the wafer sample needed for further evaluation or retention?
branches: Yes - Return sample to storage or schedule additional evaluation (back to A1 or hold)
No - Flag sample for disposal and proceed to A7

decisions.condition: Is the disposal request approved by Lab Manager?
branches: Approved - Proceed to A9 for disposal execution
Rejected - Return to Process Engineer for revision or reclassification (back to A7)

exceptions: Sample lost or damaged during transport - triggers incident report and re-evaluation of transfer process
Sample mislabeled or misidentified - requires reconciliation before evaluation proceeds
Disposal request rejected due to regulatory non-compliance - escalates to compliance team
Evaluation equipment unavailable - causes delay and requires rescheduling
Sample required unexpectedly after disposal request is submitted - requires cancellation of disposal request and re-routing

automation_opportunities.target: A1 - Identify Wafer Sample Transfer Need
automation_opportunities.rationale: Evaluation schedules and sample inventory data are typically structured and digital; an automated trigger can generate transfer requests when evaluation events are scheduled, reducing manual identification effort.
constraints: Sample tracking system must have real-time inventory visibility
Evaluation scheduling system must be integrated with sample tracking system

automation_opportunities.target: A3 - Log Sample Transfer in System
automation_opportunities.rationale: Transfer logging is a repetitive, rule-based data entry task. Barcode or RFID scanning at transfer points can automate location updates without manual entry.
constraints: Physical scanning infrastructure must be available at transfer checkpoints

automation_opportunities.rationale: If evaluation results contain structured pass/fail or threshold-based criteria, automated classification rules can flag samples for disposal or retention without full manual review, surfacing only edge cases to engineers.
constraints: Evaluation criteria must be formally defined and digitized
Human oversight required for ambiguous results

automation_opportunities.target: D1 - Is the wafer sample needed for further evaluation or retention?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Rule-based decision logic can automate this branching based on structured evaluation outcomes and predefined retention policies, reducing engineer decision burden for clear-cut cases.
constraints: Policy rules must be formally encoded
Exceptions and edge cases must still route to human review

automation_opportunities.rationale: Once samples are flagged for disposal, the disposal request form can be auto-populated using sample metadata, reducing manual data entry and accelerating request initiation.
constraints: Disposal request system must support API or data integration with sample tracking system

automation_opportunities.target: A8 - Review and Approve Disposal Request
automation_opportunities.rationale: Routine disposal requests meeting all compliance criteria can be auto-approved or fast-tracked with a simplified digital sign-off workflow, reducing bottlenecks at the Lab Manager level.
constraints: Regulatory and safety requirements may mandate human approval regardless of automation
High-risk sample categories must always require manual approval

automation_opportunities.target: A10 - Update Sample Inventory and Close Records
automation_opportunities.rationale: Disposal confirmation can automatically trigger inventory updates and record closure in the sample tracking system, eliminating a manual post-disposal data entry step.
constraints: Disposal request system and sample tracking system must be integrated
Audit trail requirements must be preserved

assumptions: Sample tracking is performed using a digital system capable of recording location, status, and transfer history.
Evaluation is conducted in a designated evaluation area separate from the sample storage location.
Disposal requires explicit managerial approval before execution, implying a formal approval workflow exists.
Disposal policies and compliance requirements are defined but assumed to be internal to the organization and not externally regulated at a level requiring third-party sign-off.
The disposal request process is distinct from the transfer process and managed through a separate or integrated system.
Transfer frequency is assumed to be event-driven based on evaluation scheduling rather than on a fixed time interval.
Samples may be retained after evaluation if they are deemed useful for future reference or additional testing.
Material handling for physical transport is a manual activity due to the physical nature of wafer samples.
RFID or barcode infrastructure availability is assumed possible but not confirmed, affecting confidence in A3 automation.

missing_information.gap: No roles or responsible parties are identified for initiating sample transfers, performing evaluations, or submitting disposal requests.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing which roles (e.g., lab technician, process engineer, quality team) own each step, it is impossible to assess handoff points, automation boundaries, or where human judgment is required.

missing_information.gap: No systems or tools are mentioned for tracking sample location, evaluation results, or disposal requests.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation feasibility depends heavily on whether a lab information management system, ERP, or tracking system exists; without this, integration opportunities cannot be assessed.

missing_information.gap: The criteria for determining which samples are 'unnecessary' after evaluation are not defined.
missing_information.why_it_matters: This is a key branching decision in the workflow. Without explicit rules or thresholds, it cannot be automated or even consistently reconstructed from event logs.

missing_information.gap: The inputs required to initiate a sample transfer (e.g., request form, work order, evaluation schedule) are not specified.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Identifying trigger documents or data inputs is essential for determining whether initiation can be automated and what data must be captured at the start of the process.

missing_information.gap: The outputs of the disposal request process (e.g., disposal record, certificate, log entry) are not described.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Knowing the required outputs determines traceability and compliance needs, which directly affect automation design and audit trail requirements.

missing_information.gap: The volume and frequency of sample transfers and disposal requests are unknown.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation ROI assessment requires understanding how often these processes occur; low-frequency manual processes may not justify automation investment.

missing_information.gap: No exception scenarios are described, such as what happens if a sample is lost during transfer, fails evaluation, or if a disposal request is rejected.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception handling logic is critical for process completeness; unhandled exceptions in automation can cause process failures or compliance issues.

missing_information.gap: It is unclear whether the disposal request requires any approval steps, regulatory sign-off, or safety review before samples are disposed of.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Approval chains introduce human-in-the-loop requirements and potential delays that must be explicitly modeled; missing this could lead to non-compliant automation.

missing_information.gap: The specific manual steps involved in physically moving samples and completing disposal requests are not described.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Identifying manual touchpoints is essential to quantify automation potential and determine which steps are candidates for robotic process automation or workflow orchestration.

missing_information.gap: It is unknown whether historical event logs or records exist for sample transfers and disposal requests.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Process mining requires historical data; if no structured logs exist, alternative discovery methods must be used and automation baselines cannot be established.

missing_information.gap: The relationship between the evaluation schedule and sample transfer timing is not defined, nor whether downstream processes depend on disposal completion.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Process dependencies affect sequencing logic and integration design; undocumented dependencies can cause bottlenecks or race conditions in an automated workflow.

missing_information.gap: No information is provided about regulatory or safety standards governing wafer sample handling and disposal.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Semiconductor wafer samples may be subject to material safety or environmental regulations; these constraints shape what can be automated and what requires human oversight.

clarification_questions.question: Who initiates a sample transfer request, and what information or trigger (e.g., evaluation schedule, work order) is required to start the process?
What specific criteria or rules determine whether a sample is classified as 'unnecessary' and eligible for disposal after evaluation?
Is there an approval workflow for disposal requests, and if so, who must approve it and under what conditions can it be rejected?
What systems or tools are currently used to track sample locations, record evaluation results, and manage disposal requests?
How frequently do sample transfers and disposal requests occur, and are there peak periods or batch patterns in this process?
What regulatory or safety requirements govern the physical handling and disposal of wafer samples, and do these impose mandatory manual steps?
